title: AWS Batch on Fargate, Step Functions and Lambda: who does what

questions.stem: A planner submits a scenario of the large portfolio with a 40-minute solver limit. In the lesson's design, which service runs the solve itself?

options.text: A Lambda function, because it starts in seconds and may use up to 10,240 MB of memory
options.says: Lambda runs a function for at most 900 seconds (15 minutes); the lesson keeps it to short glue, never the solve.

options.text: A Batch job on Fargate, because the job's own timeout is the only bound on its time
options.says: Right: Batch on Fargate solves; a job's timeout (at least 60 s) is its only time bound.

options.text: A chain of Lambda calls, which Step Functions restarts after their 900 seconds run out
options.says: The page: a function stopped at 15 minutes leaves no result at all, so Lambda never solves; Step Functions waits for a Batch job.

options.text: The API's own process, because lesson 12.4.2's thread pool already runs each solve as a job
options.says: The API answers in milliseconds and does none of the waiting; each solve gets its own container.

origin.section: Each Service Does the Part It Is Built For

questions.stem: A run's solver time limit is 30 minutes. How does the lesson set the Batch job's timeout for that run?

options.text: At 30 minutes, so Batch ends the job at the same point as the search itself ends
options.says: If the two were equal, Batch could kill the worker while it writes the result, losing a plan the solver found.

options.text: Under 30 minutes, so Batch's retry restarts the job before the search gives up
options.says: The documentation says a job stopped by its timeout is not retried; and it writes nothing.

options.text: Over 30 minutes, because Batch retries a job it stopped, with the minutes left
options.says: A job stopped by its timeout is not retried, by the RegisterJobDefinition reference the lesson cites.

options.text: Over 30 minutes, so the worker can still write its best plan after the search ends
options.says: Right: the solver stops at its limit and writes its best plan; Batch's timeout is only the backstop, with margin.

origin.section: A Job Definition Fixes the Image, Size, Timeout and Retries; a Submission Names the Run

questions.stem: The API's call to start run-0042 times out, and it calls start_execution again with the same name and the same input while the first execution is still running. What happens?

options.text: Step Functions returns the execution it started before, so only one solve job is submitted
options.says: Right: for a Standard workflow, the same name and input as a running execution return that execution.

options.text: Step Functions starts a second execution, and Batch's client token drops the duplicate job
options.says: SubmitJob takes no client token; the lesson says the same call sent twice starts two jobs.

options.text: Step Functions refuses the call with ExecutionAlreadyExists, so the API retries under a new name
options.says: ExecutionAlreadyExists is for the same name with different input, or a closed execution.

options.text: Step Functions starts a second execution, and the conditional result write drops the duplicate
options.says: The same name and input return the running execution instead of starting another.
